strengths: QuEST addresses a useful computer-vision problem: reducing diffusion-model quantization costs while retaining usable low-bit generation. Selectively finetuning temporal and attention-related layers, together with activation scales, is a practical contribution; the reported trainable subset is below 7% for LDM-4.

The reported improvements are substantial in several settings. On LSUN-Bedrooms, W4A4 FID improves from EfficientDM’s 10.60 to 5.64; on LSUN-Churches, it improves from 14.34 to 11.76. W4A8 Bedrooms FID reaches 3.26 versus 5.37 for Q-Diffusion and 2.95 for full precision. These gains have value even without matching full-precision quality everywhere.

The experiments cover unconditional, class-conditional, and text-conditioned generation, with additional CIFAR-10 and TFMQ-DM comparisons in the supplement. Table 6 supports the usefulness of both alignment components, reducing FID from 6.95 to 4.41 and then 3.26; Table 7 supports combining local and global supervision.

The pipeline is generally understandable, and activation-distribution plots and sensitivity experiments provide useful empirical motivation. The manuscript links code, attributes datasets and baseline methods, and includes a relevant discussion of possible effects on watermarking and safety checks.
weaknesses: The theoretical argument contains substantive errors. For the stated MSE on final-layer outputs, a second-order Taylor expansion is exact regardless of perturbation magnitude, so large perturbations alone do not establish Proposition 3.1. Furthermore, Eq. (10) replaces the incremental quadratic terms involving epsilon in Eq. (11) with cumulative output-residual terms without justification. Although Section 3.4 explicitly disclaims a performance guarantee, the stated theorem does not establish the claimed explanation for finetuning. This weakens the theoretical contribution without directly invalidating the empirical method.

The central efficiency claim is difficult to assess consistently. Table 6 reports 15.25 GPU-hours for QuEST, whereas Table 8 reports 0.45 hours on LDM-4, with different resulting FIDs. The manuscript does not reconcile the settings or clearly separate calibration generation, quantization initialization, and finetuning costs. A consistent accounting is necessary to establish the actual efficiency advantage. Model-size estimates also do not demonstrate inference acceleration; no measured inference latency is supplied.

The closest baseline needs more convincing validation. Table 3 reports EfficientDM generation failure at W8A8 on both LSUN datasets, despite successful W4A4 generation; on Bedrooms, its W4A8 FID is substantially worse than W4A4 FID, 15.15 versus 10.60. These outcomes are not necessarily impossible, but require diagnostic explanation and documented configurations because they underpin important comparative claims.

The evidence for low-bit quality preservation is incomplete. Stable Diffusion is evaluated quantitatively only with CLIP Score, which does not establish visual fidelity or diversity. On ImageNet, W4A4 IS drops from 364.73 to 202.45 while FID improves markedly. The paper recognizes this metric disagreement, but does not resolve it with a stronger fidelity/diversity assessment. The results support improved W4A4 viability more clearly than broad preservation of generation quality.

The distinctive selection and progression choices are not sufficiently isolated. Temporal sensitivity and efficient quantization-aware finetuning already appear in cited prior work. The component additions in Table 6 are helpful, but parameter- and compute-matched alternative layer selections, and joint versus progressive optimization, would establish whether the proposed choices provide benefits beyond allocating additional optimization capacity.

Important reproducibility details remain unspecified in the manuscript: exact trainable-layer lists, quantizer granularity, gradient handling through quantization, batch sizes, and training schedules for each stage and model. The code link is helpful, but these omissions also make the reported parameter fractions, baseline configurations, and efficiency comparisons difficult to assess independently.
